messages:
alex_ae: Heads up team: ZenithHealth POC hit a hard stop. Their security team will only allow connections authenticated with client certificates to upstream endpoints. They explicitly refuse to rely on IP allowlists unless we can provide cert-based auth as well. Any options for Dedicated endpoints short-term?

kevin_sales: Zenith is on a tight timeline for a week-long evaluation. Procurement won't approve a customer-facing proxy. They want minimal configuration on their side.

taylor_se: Short answer: Dedicated can give you stable egress IPs, but we don't currently expose mutual TLS client-auth out-of-the-box for hosted/dedicated control plane endpoints. Private (VPC or on-prem) supports mTLS for ingress in our private deployment. For a one-week POC we have two practical approaches: (A) Reserve static NAT IPs for the Dedicated pool and provide allowlist + short test, or (B) issue a temporary client cert that our gateway will accept for the POC and revoke after. Approach B requires an exception.

zenith-netops: Approach A is simpler for us from a firewall perspective. But Security insists on cert auth in addition to IP allowlisting. They want defense-in-depth.

jo_infra: We can reserve a /32 pair (two IPs) from our NAT block for the POC. ETA ~6 hours. If they require both IP allowlist + client cert pinning, infra can also configure a temporary TLS listener that checks a client cert against a pinned fingerprint. That is not automated; it's a manual change and requires sign-off from security.

pat_security: Manual pinning policy: for POC only, we can accept a PEM client cert fingerprint pinned at the edge. Must document issuance, expiration (max 7 days), revocation procedure, and get an approved risk waiver. If infra is doing manual TLS config, include audit entries in the waiver.

alex_ae: Can someone paste the sample firewall snippet and the curl test for cert auth we can give Zenith?

jo_infra: Sample allowlist stanza (send to Zenith firewall team):

```
# ZenithHealth - Redwood Dedicated POC allowlist
203.0.113.10/32  # nat egress ip primary
203.0.113.11/32  # nat egress ip secondary
# destination: dedicated-zenith.pool.redwood.ai (443)
```

jo_infra: Minimal curl client-cert test (if we enable temporary cert):

```
curl -v --cacert redwood-ca.pem \\
  --cert zenith-client.pem --key zenith-client.key \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <DEDICATED-API-KEY>" \\
  https://dedicated-zenith.pool.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
```

pat_security: Checklist for cert-pinning POC: 1) Zenith generates CSR and sends to Redwood in secure transfer; 2) Redwood issues short-lived client cert (<=7 days); 3) Infra pins fingerprint on gateway; 4) Test connectivity; 5) Revoke cert at POC end and remove pin. I'll prepare waiver template.

taylor_se: If Zenith cannot create a CSR quickly, we can issue a pre-generated client cert but that raises more security flags. Prefer customer-controlled CSR.

kevin_sales: Zenith asked about rotation. For POC we'll do a single rotation mid-week if needed. Also asked about logging: they want to see TLS client auth succeeded logs. Is that accessible?

pat_security: We can surface auth success/failure events in the audit logs but granular logs will be redacted. We can provide a signed statement of auth events for the POC timeframe.

jo_infra: Action items: infra to reserve 2 IPs (ticket INF-4907). Security to draft waiver (SEC-POC-73). Sales/AE to get CSR preference from Zenith. SE to prep test steps. I'll kick off ticket now.

deploy-bot: [ticket] INF-4907 created by jo_infra - reserved nat 203.0.113.10, 203.0.113.11

alex_ae: Scheduling a call with Zenith tomorrow 09:00 PT to confirm CSR vs pre-generated certs. Kevin, can you invite "zenith-sec@zenhealth.com" and include the sample allowlist?

kevin_sales: On it. I'll attach the allowlist and the curl example.

zenith-netops: Thanks, please also include the exact commonName format we should use in the CSR so our PKI team can auto-issue.

taylor_se: Use CN=zenith-poc-client and SAN with the Zenith team email as a URI if their PKI requires it. We'll accept RSA2048 or ECDSA P-256.

alex_ae: Great. We'll try static IPs + cert pinning for defense-in-depth. If that fails, pivot to Private/VPC later. Thanks everyone. :+1:
